A.cap: A big-character poster board in 1966. Most of the people reading it are workers.
A.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1966 No. 10, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

B.alt: The old sign of the Wing On Company in Shanghai being knocked down, November 1966
B.cap: November 1966. The old sign of the Wing On Company on Nanjing Road, Shanghai, has been knocked down. The street below is full of people.
B.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1966 No. 11–12, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

C.cap: Early 1967, Shanghai rebels on the march. The banner hails the telegram of congratulations from the Party Central Committee, the State Council, the Central Military Commission and the Central Cultural Revolution Group to the revolutionary rebel groups of Shanghai.
C.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1967, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

D.alt: The founding of the Shanghai Revolutionary Committee
D.cap: The hall at the founding of the Shanghai Revolutionary Committee. The sign above reads Long Live the Communist Party of China.
D.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1967, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

E.alt: A mass meeting at the Port of Shanghai, 1967
E.cap: 1967, a mass meeting at the Port of Shanghai. The rails of the passenger ship are hung with slogans.
E.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1967, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

F.cap: 1967, a study board inside Yangshupu Power Plant. In January the plant's coal stock nearly ran out.
F.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1967, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

G.cap: Shanghai railway station in 1967. Several passenger trains stand on the sidings.
G.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1967, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

H.credit: Image: China Pictorial, July 1967, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

I.alt: Wang Hongwen delivering a report at the Tenth Party Congress
I.cap: August 24, 1973. Wang Hongwen delivers the report on revising the Party constitution at the Tenth Party Congress.
I.credit: Image: Xinhua, The Tenth National Congress of the Party of Unity and Victory, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

L.alt: Slogans on the Fudan University campus, 1976
L.cap: Spring 1976, slogans on the Fudan University campus: “Defend the Party Center with our blood and our lives.”
L.credit: Image: photographer unknown, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

M.alt: The old buildings of No. 17 State Cotton Mill
M.cap: The old buildings of No. 17 State Cotton Mill, now the Shanghai International Fashion Center. 2024.
M.credit: Image: 向史公哲曰, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

N.alt: The joint rebel team of No. 9 State Cotton Mill, 1967
N.cap: 1967, a joint rebel rally at a state cotton mill. The front row holds a sign for the No. 9 State Cotton Mill Joint Rebel Team.
N.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1967, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

O.alt: The spinning shop of a textile mill, 1967
O.cap: 1967, the spinning shop of No. 9 State Cotton Mill.
O.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1967, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

S.alt: Educated youth sent to the countryside, 1964
S.cap: 1964, educated youth sent to the countryside walk along a field ridge with hoes on their shoulders.
S.credit: Image: China Pictorial, 1964 No. 4, public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

V.alt: Nixon's party at Shanghai airport, February 1972
V.cap: February 1972. Nixon's party walks down the stairs at Shanghai airport past a portrait of Mao Zedong.
V.credit: Image: U.S. National Archives (Nixon Library), public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
